details:
Q1: When cycles are exhausted and a high or critical finding is still open, what should happen once the bounded fix and re-audit budget is also spent? The budget is the existing `fix` retries, capped by `MAX_REVIEW_BLOCKED_RETRIES`, and each fix earns one more audit cycle.
Choices:
A) Hold the PR and never merge it. Turn a judge `merge` / `merge_with_followup` into `fix` while fix retries remain. In the final round, label the PR `ai:security-pass-failed` plus `ai:review-blocked`, send a CRITICAL alert, and leave the PR open until a clean audit of the current head or a human decision. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Same as A while retries remain, but in the final round automatically use `close_and_reissue`, so a replacement issue starts again from the preserved baseline.
C) Never auto-fix. Only refuse the merge (`judge_action=security_hold`) and leave the next step to the judge's other options or to a human.
Q2: Which findings should block the merge?
Choices:
A) `high` and `critical`, plus any finding whose severity is missing or not recognised (fail closed). `medium` and `low` can still merge, with follow-up issues as they do today. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Only findings that state `high` or `critical`. Unknown severity is treated as non-blocking.
C) Every open finding, whatever its severity. The audit must be clean before any merge.
Q3: Should this change also cover the orchestrator's project-level exhaustion judge? That judge can use `accept_with_followup` to waive high or critical findings (`security_pass_exhaustion_judge` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, plus `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_KEEP_FIXING_ROUNDS`, which turns `keep_fixing` into `accept_with_followup`).
Choices:
A) No. Limit the change to the single-issue review-blocked judge path the finding cites (`scripts/review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh` / `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh`), and file the orchestrator path as a separate issue if needed. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Yes. Apply the same severity block to the orchestrator path in the same change, so the exhaustion judge and the keep-fixing cap can never waive high or critical findings.
